note: The queue is the culture's central fact, not a custom inside it: the plough, the roof and the levy are three claims on the same hands, so this clan exists as the one household obligation that survives all three.
Distance is not conserved here, so a tenure claim is a queue and not a measurement, which is why the family has a number and not a boundary.
The only watercourse on the plains moves its bed far enough between floods to relocate every settlement on it, so this clan's slot is revoked about once a generation and re-earned rather than owned.
The dues are the whole obligation line on the far side of the ford, and a household with no cultivator left pays them out of a crop it has to reach across a river that will not be where it was.
An oath sworn at a crossing has to be re-earned against a river that will not be where it was; this clan's whole tenure is an oath of exactly that kind, so the rule is a supply line to them.
The queue was full when the stair opened, so this clan supplied the movement instead of making it: their surplus households went up and their slot stayed where it was.
This line is the household that gave the culture its subject: a partner left behind when the cultivators went up the stair, with a name still attached and nobody in it.
The run relocates every settlement on it between floods, so this line is the one family on the plains whose address is a course rather than a place.
The movement was economic before it was spiritual, so the people it did not move are the ones the plains had to invent a household for.
The Assembly meets at the crossing rather than beside it because that is the only boundary fact anybody here can prove; a family with kin on both banks has no other civic form available.
The dues are collected at a ford the absent used to work, so this line pays a toll levied on a memory it cannot stop anybody from having.
One holds the name, one holds the dues, and the charter of the run recognises both and pays neither twice. The quarrel is over which of the two the absent would have claimed first.
The same absence read the other way: this line holds the estate the absent left rather than the name, which is the reading the culture permits because it counts nothing twice either.
A threshing floor needs ground that will hold a season, and this is the only tier-low ground where a claim on a harvest can be enforced at all.
Grain is the only accepted payment for a crossing, so the crop this line collects is the setting's only durable wealth and the tariff is what it collects it for.
The standing agreement is that a crossing is paid in grain and never in coin, and a household holding the standing grain claim has more to lose from a coin tariff than anybody in the setting.
Arrival at the stair's foot is repeatable and departure is not, so a stranger's first act here is a transaction; this line supplies the grain that transaction is settled in.
The floor has to be downstream of wherever the flood currently is, so this line's ledger is rewritten each season at a place the river chooses.

The cull was this house's own instrument, applied to its own siblings, because a line held pure inside one household concentrates faster than the same line spread across a village and debt was the only lever it had.

The narrowed concentration descends from the household that narrowed the pool. It was selected under cultivation debt, never designed, which is why its grant is sustained rather than sudden and crosses races freely.

The March charter names this line for the River Lantern and the seat has been vacant two generations, so the house is heir to an office its own arithmetic emptied. The vacancy is not an oversight; it is this household's arithmetic.

This clan is the mechanism the culture describes: cull the branches, bind every survivor to a named debt before first breath was drawn cold, and keep the concentration by never paying for a second line.
The culled line crossed races freely, so it is found wherever the shelf's households had already taken in somebody else, and the shelf is the one ground with a living record of the mixing.

One house's founding act was a recorded pairing repeated until it crossed a race line; the other's founding act was refusing to pair at all. They hold the same argument about dilution from opposite ends and neither will move.

The host half of this kinship is not a descent but a signed partnership with a body that can leave, so the household's bloodline is a document renewed each generation and the line is what both parties signed.
The thorn is native to the mortal plains and a host can only be renewed where the host's own law budget lets a body survive at all, so the pairing is a low-tier contract.

A symbiote that has to be kept near fire to hold its shape can only be hosted where elemental law is written, and the only ground on this side that writes it is Flame Valley, one pass away from anybody's market.

Re-mastering a symbol every generation so nothing built can be read by a later technique is the same discipline as re-signing a pairing every generation so no dead host's contract survives into a body that never agreed to it.

The hybrid is the whole economic point of the pairing: without it the host is carrying a share it cannot use and the thorn is a liability, so this household's standing is entirely downstream of somebody else taking the other side.
The Dao is read differently per world, so a bond valid in one composition is not valid in the next; the clause that makes a host pairing portable between tiers is the clause that makes it revocable.

A lifespan that outlasts three centuries of predecessors is the entire cause of this household's headlessness: authority cannot be personal to somebody whose own memory of the household's decisions has expired.
The long-lived are native to the spirit peaks and not to the plains, which is why this clan is a tier-up family and not a plains one: its body needs a composition the lower frame cannot seat.

A body that outlives its own century needs a clock that keeps time, and temporal law is the only thing in the book that writes one. Seat it and this household could exist anywhere; leave it unwritten and the clan is stuck on the peaks.

The society re-cuts itself every year because a promise that can be inherited quietly is not a promise. A household with three centuries of living members is exactly the inheritance it refuses to be, so its members attend instead of claiming.
The long line started as an ordinary settled hearth household and lengthened over centuries of not dying, which is why it is still carrying the most common concentration in the setting.

The repeated salt-and-tide pairing is what produced this household, and the document that proves it is also the document that files them under a race they have spent four generations being corrected out of.
A household whose civic vocabulary is high, low or turning cannot describe itself as one people or two, so the tideline's refusal to count inside and outside is what keeps this pairing legible.
The shelf is the only ground where the survey that files this family as a different race is itself written down, so it is the only place they can appeal.
The crosser's body reads the brine without harm, so it is the only pairing on the shelf whose children can crew a tailings boat; the underwriter buys that tolerance rather than the strength.
The dominion's territory is exactly its waterline, so a household straddling salt and tide is domiciled nowhere at all and can only be reached by following the line.

A house that founded itself on refusing to pair and a house that founded itself on repeating a pairing are arguing about the same dilution from opposite ends, and the argument is over who gets to call the result a family.

The discipline spends a furnace deliberately and closes permanently the moment the body is lit. Closing cannot be unlearned, so the contract is taken at naming inside a household and not taught in a school anybody may leave.

Elemental law is never written below the spirit tier, so a fire-affinity body has no budget to spend into and must burn its own reserve. This whole household form is a response to an absent law, not to a shortage.

The famine was the demographic shape of this house's arithmetic: a population whose fuel is its own body, thinning at exactly the rate it could not stop, and every signature here is an attempt to slow that rate.

The founding concentration descends from this household's first signed burn. The grant is defensive and continuous because a slower burn is the only thing a furnace with nothing seated beneath it can be asked to do.
A fire affinity with no elemental seat beneath it is an asset on Flame Valley and a liability everywhere else, which is the whole reason this house's members are signed rather than trained.
The three seated laws are exactly what iron, a plant and a beast need, so a plains household is the tier where a signed furnace is the most reliable inheritance available and the least profitable.

A face shift has to be worked by a body that can stand at it without burning through one shift, and only a signed furnace survives one shift, so the lease clan buys the contract rather than the strength.
The culture is not a people but a scar behaving like one, and this lineage is the scar's household form: it holds the eating rules of the year there was nothing rather than a memory of the year.

Speed bought out of lifespan is a demographic curve, and a curve does not stop when the shortage does. This household is that curve's survivors, still eating to a rule that stopped being necessary a century ago.

The mortuary line reads the famine's dead as one declared group each year, and this household's portioning rules are the same device at table scale: a rule that assigns rather than a feeling that mourns.

The college reads a life against the ceiling its frame had already spent before the person was born, and this household is entered under that reading, which is the only record of its kind it will ever have.
The scar is bounded to the tier where the arithmetic held: a fifty-year body on a frame that seats three laws has nowhere else to be and no other frame to migrate to.
The composition that closed every gate is the reason this household's rule is a ceiling: a body that must spend its own reserve has no gate left to spend it toward.

One exhausted seam cost the mortal tier its whole ladder, because no spatial law was seated to open fresh rock. Every household working that face lost its work inside one generation, and the ones with nothing left took the dead ground as an estate.
The worked-out face yields nothing and cannot be occupied, so it is the only ground on the plains nobody will contest and therefore the only claim a grief-struck household can hold without a fight.
The guild works the last unworked iron, and every survey this household keeps is a survey that names where the seam is not. The contention is over a resource that is already gone.

The flats are worth holding only while the seam is being worked, so the argument over which side of it a household may live on is exactly this: the lease needs shift, the heirs need the ground left alone.

A split tally is the only evidence a river community can carry, dispute and destroy without a scribe, and after the grief the ground held no other record, so the claim on a dead seam is kept in halves.
The heap is the ore that is gone, still standing on the ground that cut it, so this clan stands on the exhausted deposit itself and its title is the number it has reduced.
A crew that owes the heap it did not move has a debt measured in barrows, which is a weight and not a distance and therefore the one accounting this tier can support at all.
Forty years of heap has to be carried out by hand before the working face can advance a foot, so the haulers are the only labour the clan has and the only thing it can be squeezed through.

With no spatial law seated there is no process on which waste disperses, so a spent seam is visible from outside. This tenancy exists because a resource can be seen to end, and that evidence has to be worked off by somebody.
A tenure queue cannot be shortened, so its surplus households go to the heap. A clan of crewmen is what a full tenure queue produces when there is nothing else on the ground to hand them.
The face cannot advance until the heap is gone, so every barrow this clan removes is a barrow of shift the lease clan does not pay for. The two tenancies are permanently in each other's way.
The lease is on a working face, and the only ground here that a body can be paid to stand on is the last unworked iron, which is what makes the flats a country at all.
Nothing native to this tier is licensed to work a face, so the clan pays the admission charge to stand on its own claim and to watch a trial it is not allowed to attempt.
Holding the face holds the deposit, so the guild staffs the lease rather than owning it and can lose a shift to a crew that will not answer a standing order.

Flatswatch is a garrison holding ground its own faction cannot staff from, because every soul inside the walls is a visitor from a world with a larger law budget. This clan is one of those visitors, holding a lease.

A mortal world spends all three slots on physical, life and qi, so elemental, spatial and temporal are never written and no humanoid is admissible here. The lease exists because its holder is a foreigner on his own ground.
The lease needs the heap gone and the heap is somebody else's debt. Neither tenancy can advance without the other losing, which is the arrangement that keeps both families alive and neither solvent.
The culture holds the year's dead together as a declared group because a fifty-year body produces no growing store of the long-lived. This lineage is the kinship form of that declaration.

Elemental law is never seated beneath a fire-affinity body on this tier, so every overflow is absorbed by flesh that cannot be repaired. Seat the law and this household form stops being necessary, which is why it is a response and not a culture.
The famine made every individual short of fuel and the shortfall collective at once. A group that dies together is the only record a shortening body can keep, so the group is the lineage.

The college reads the dead as the frame said and not as the village remembers, and it keeps the divergence rather than resolving it. This household supplies most of the readings and has no vote on any of them.
The affinity whose fuel is its own furnace is what makes the fifty-year body, and the fifty-year body is what makes a declared group the only durable unit of kinship here.
The plains are the tier where the life-law seat is already spent keeping plants and beasts coherent, so nobody here is licensed to live long enough to need a different kind of record.

The culture has no temples and no museum because a great ascension is a fire-affinity body opened on a purpose; it has a register, and the register is the only relic it keeps. This household is the register's address.
The vault is cut into the heap, so its doors are spoil that has never moved. Dead ground is where this setting keeps its records, which is why the record is kept here and not in a town.
The vault has no door that opens onto worked ground, so everything a reading produces has to be carried past the heap before it is a recovery anybody can file.
Realms five through nine are the whole remaining mortal ladder closed by a limit nobody was fighting, and this is the household whose page records which attempt stopped where.

The densest bodies in the setting stop at realm seventeen, one gate short, and only one account survives and it is a stonecutter's. The register is the only other place the attempts are recorded, and it disagrees with the account.

A failed ascent injures the ground as well as the body, and the reading is published, so the reading names exactly who has nowhere to go. The household cannot read a loss aloud without taking in the debris's children.
No descent connects them. The line forms by intake at a reading, which is why the register household is the ancestor here and why the register had to be publishable in the first place.

The culture records the whole recovery publicly and never displays a fragment again; these children are the part of the recovery that could still be carried off by somebody, which is why they are entered on the page.
The vault is cut into spoil, so the ground under this household is the debris of the attempts it is named for and moves whenever the heap is moved.
The mortal ladder's last gates were shut from the inside by the frame, and every attempt near a gate injured the ground. This is the household form of a law ceiling that keeps producing orphans.
Two lineages with no descent and no shared disaster, built the same way: both are fifty-year populations whose natural increase failed, so both replace birth with intake and neither can concentrate.
A body that dies of a shortage decades before it dies of age leaves the fertile years empty and the dependents full, so the households that survived were the ones with survivors to take in.
The households that kept the portioning rules were the only ones with a table left to fill, so the intake followed the rule: a child was taken in when the worst year's allowance said there was room.
The dead are held as a declared group rather than a growing roll, so an adopted child and a born child are entered identically and neither line can claim seniority from the arrangement.
The affinity that burns its own reserve is what empties the fertile years; without it this household would be a normal one and the adoption would never have been necessary.
Adoption is a low-tier answer. A fifty-year body cannot carry an heir upward, so the households that took children in are the ones that could never send their own out.

Distance is not conserved on the plains, so a road that measures itself is the only repeatable departure there. This household is the constituency that measurement created: raised on the route, by the term.

A household holding a standing crop claim cannot feed the ones who left, so the leaving went up the stair and this line counts those children as lost rather than as gone. That is the whole of its descent.

The toll-town's entire population is visitors, including its own officers, because arrival is repeatable and departure is not. A household of arrivals is the only family the town can actually contain.

The only door out of a world that licenses nobody to enter it fills with unlicensed arrivals, and a queue of bodies is the one thing that must not become a fight. These households are the people standing in it.

A term on the stair is priced as passage, and passage denominated in a body's own upkeep is the only wealth anybody can hold between tiers, so a term-holder's household is paid in the one thing it cannot carry.
The stair was the only departure the ascent ever used, and these are the people it fed on the way. The movement's constituency is not a village; it is a queue.

A maximally dense fixed body forms the cavity it needs at seventeen and cannot form the next one, so the setting's largest supply of competent strangers is made of people who reached the end and stayed there.
Six seats against exactly six laws and no redundancy is the frame in which a fixed dense body has nothing left to form, so this household is a human consequence of a composition, not of a defeat.

A fixed dense body can carry and lift in a way nothing else here can, and the same density closes what a qi technique needs open. The guild paid for a second shorter ladder, and this household supplies it by stopping at seventeen.
The quarry is the only verifiable hole in the setting, so the work that has to be done there is work that needs a body with no next gate and no interest in leaving.
The company's product is a falling number held in public, so it needs carriers who will stay for a measurement that takes a generation and cannot be improved from inside.
Fifteen seats over six groups is a load and not a resource, and a household whose members cannot advance is the human form of the same arithmetic: capacity that cannot be spent on anybody.

The charter names this line and the cull left it one thread. That is the whole of the descent and the whole of the vacancy: an arithmetic decision about money, made inside a household, outlived the office it was meant to fill.
The seat is unfilled for two generations and written as existing with no value rather than as a zero, so the line is heir to a third state and can neither be used nor written off.
Every appointment passes a trial the naming office cannot judge, so a named line is a candidate and never an appointee. Two generations of vacancy is what that rule costs this household and no other.
The Lantern is a river office and the run relocates every settlement on it, so the household's own address moves and the charter's named line does not. The vacancy is stable; the river is not.

The Marshal commands nothing that can be counted and has authority over passage only, so a line that owes its standing to a charter rather than to an appointment is exactly the sort of subject it can hold without owning.

The Regent may name a seat and may not take one, and this household is the named line for a seat nobody has filled. A naming office is the only party in the setting with an interest in closing that gap quietly.
The vacancies are physical: a seat nobody has ever filled is an engraved absence visible from the district below. Holding an inherited vacancy means standing on the engraving and being seen to.

Nine vacant seats at the top and four below, and no procedure capable of certifying any of them empty. That is why unclaimed capacity pays its own upkeep and why this household's asset cannot be priced.

The office names the unfilled high seats and is forbidden to take them, so it holds the only register of which terraces have never been filled. This household's claim is whatever that register says and nothing more.
The council decides who may step onto the nine terraces and cannot be a candidate for any of them. A household holding a claim to a step is barred by construction from the only body that grants one.

Fifteen imprints over three layers leave nine surplus imprints, and a surplus seat is indistinguishable from an unfilled one until somebody stands on it. This family is the standing-on-it that never happens.

The rule that the highest office may name a seat and may not take one, and that every appointment passes a trial it cannot judge, is what keeps this household's vacancy a vacancy instead of a succession.
The same density that closes what a qi technique needs open is what a cold-bathing guild built its own currency on, and this household holds the object that currency was first struck from.

A forge ground needs an open sky and a rising current, and three of its grounds are on tiers where elemental law is unspent and the fire never takes. Holding one is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

Realms three and four turned on metallurgy: a core has to be caged in something, so the third gate was a mining problem long before it was a spiritual one. This household is the archive of the object that solved it.
Iron on the mortal plains is the only dense material a core can be caged in, and that bed is now spent. The line's charge is downstream of a resource the tier has already run out of.
The guild works the last unworked iron, and a household whose entire standing is one piece of smelted iron is not a household the guild can move, buy out or wait out.

Spending a furnace before it overflows is the discipline that produced the founding smelt, and the household that guards the relic is the last place the discipline is kept as an object rather than as a practice.

The window is set by the Tidemark season rather than by the holder's preference, which is the only arrangement that makes a toll defensible and a timetable not. This dynasty's whole office is the refusal to set it.

The undertow frame writes spatial and temporal law, so a pass can be surveyed, closed and reopened on a published date. The calendar this dynasty publishes is a direct product of the seats that frame carries.

Galehold holds the only crossing and its calendar is not its own: the holder sets the price and never the date, which is a distinction the polity can only survive if one household refuses to be given the date.
A pass can only be surveyed, closed and reopened on a published date where temporal law is written, so this office exists exactly one tier above where it is needed and cannot be moved down.
The household that left the plains first and kept both claims came up the ridge and found that the only durable power on this side was the calendar, not the ground.

Ground sets the price and the calendar sets the date, so the two houses have argued about price for three generations without ever contesting the schedule. That is the arrangement working, not a truce.

The league of the two coasts formed the moment the sea became worth owning, and a shipping date is obeyed by people who never heard of its author. This dynasty is the league's most valuable member and its least visible.

Ten seats over six groups leaves four duplicate imprints and a duplicate needs somewhere to sit, so the surplus rises through this district rather than being argued about above it. Somebody has to hold it on the way up.

The observation of a strained law only counts if it is repeated, and at the top of the setting one repetition costs a lifetime. This dynasty supplies the custodians whose standing is capacity refused.

Six groups cannot fill three, six, ten or fifteen seats, and layers are what make the larger budgets mean anything. This household's entire function exists because of that arithmetic and would be redundant in a frame with no slack.

An era whose defining political fact is a set of unfilled high seats produces the only kind of authority that can be built without filling them, and the only kind of household that can be built out of holding nothing.

One house administers the seats that exist and are spare; the other holds the seats that do not exist and are named. Neither can be given to the other without either closing a vacancy or claiming a duplicate.
One holds the imprints that exist twice and the other holds the seats that cannot be filled at all; each is the other's standing argument that the count is wrong.

Jade holds qi and will not give it up, so the cleft's best refinement ground is its worst farming ground, and whoever feeds the workings owns the mine more durably than whoever digs it. This house owns no jade at all.
The cleft is a narrow cold seam with no road to it except through the Gale Pass, so the people who provision it are the people who decide who works at all.

The holdfast is a gradient of thin, hard, increasingly deep workings that cannot grow a crop on any of them, so a food contract is the only thing that holds it together and this household is that contract.
No road reaches the cleft except through one pass, and the pass is on somebody else's calendar. This house's entire supply line is a schedule it does not keep.
Food and ore are two claims on the same series of workings, and every hour spent eating is an hour not cutting. This household is the reason the guild's shift is short.
Both profit from bodies crossing and neither can move material, which makes it the only alliance in the setting that costs nothing to keep and cannot be broken without losing the corridor.

The two deposits on the ridge are one geological accident, so every claim on stone is a claim on jade and a claim on jade is a claim on the only pass over it. Holding the pass settles all three arguments at once.

Passage is the setting's only durable wealth because it is the only supply chain whose unit is a person and nobody may levy a seat, so this house's whole income is permission to be a person somewhere else.

The pass-state holds the only crossing and sets the price and never the date. That arrangement is only possible because the ground and the calendar are held by two households who agreed to split them.
The household that climbed first took the ground on the way up, then handed the calendar to a second family on purpose, because a house holding both would make the corridor unarguable.

The office keeps debts on a tally cut with the debtor and held by both parties, so its entire instrument is unavailable to a house that grants nothing in writing. The only tool it has left is to deny the pass.
Neither side can move material and both need bodies to move, so the alliance needs no negotiation and survives every quarrel about anything else.
The setting's first choke point and the only supply route to both the jade cleft and Flame Valley, held by a household whose right of refusal is the thing that keeps it a pass instead of a wall.
The pass ground was given away on purpose and this line is what it was given to. The split is the founding act of both households, so neither can call the other a usurper.
The ground sets the price and the calendar sets the date, so the two houses dispute only what is safe to dispute. Their real argument is about which of them would be blamed for a closure.
The flock occupies the worst hours of the window, so the pass is usable only when something neither house controls has moved. Both households' standing depends on an animal's timetable.
A path is opened by two worlds agreeing on one group and by nothing else, so this household's only real asset is an agreement nobody is obliged to keep and re-surveyed every period.

The ledger is where passage became the one controllable supply chain and where the counting houses and the marshal's authority over the crossings came from, so this line's ground is worth what the ledger says a body costs.
A tenure-queue household was the only kind of family that could afford to leave and still have something to come back to, so the ascent began here and this lineage is its first branch.

One household leaving and keeping its lower claim proved the move was reversible, and that is what turned an economic push into a movement: everyone who went after them left knowing the plains were still there to lose.
Spirit stone and jade ore sit in the spirit tier and cannot be found below it, so the move was a resource decision before it was a spiritual one.

One folded ridge carries spirit stone and jade in the same bedding, and the first tier with all six law groups written is the first where a border is a line rather than a claim. This lineage is where they learned that.

A figure quoted in the plains' weights is meaningless in the peaks, so a family that could not price the move keeps both ledgers rather than convert either. This lineage is the reason the conversion was needed.
The plains license no humanoid, so a body from a world with a larger law budget is a visitor wherever it stands. This lineage pays the admission charge at the foot of its own stair.
Arrival is repeatable and departure is not, so a stranger's first act at the stair's foot is a transaction. This lineage keeps the lower half of its ledger in that town's market.

A counting house publishes credit, safe-conduct and trading posts against exclusivity, and the household behind it is where the refusals are learned. The guild is the purpose; this is the party that can be harmed by changing it.

Access is the only thing the house thinks is worth fighting over, and the tariff is the instrument that turns access into a price. Nobody may levy a seat, so this is as close to a tax as the setting permits.

The dominion's territory is exactly its waterline and the population cannot be moved up the shore without ceasing to be the people it governs, so the roads it holds are the only thing that survives the tide.
A merger would make the underwriters priceable, so the two houses settle risk by marriage instead and keep trading under an exclusivity neither of them can enforce alone.

This house can only be obeyed while every member refuses to carry a rival's goods, and that refusal needs a published list to refuse against. A house that files nothing is a house the roads cannot be applied to.

The lodge sells bodies already tuned to the frame on the far side of a tear, which is the one thing this house's exclusive roads guarantee nobody needs. The counting house's asset is safe arrival; the lodge's is not needing it.
A people that declined to price its most profitable cargo was never worth raiding, and this household inherited the same reasoning in a stronger form: it prices the roads and not the risk.
The house publishes technique, attendance and a chamber to practise in and takes discretion in return, so this household's real figures live in one head that is not permitted to write them down.
The practice is the household's whole constitution: the real figures in the head of one member, unrecorded, because a house that files everything cannot be left alone.

A currency that is not a medium at all, kept because a house with nothing written has nothing to seize, nothing to cite and nothing to lose in a raid. This household is the reason it still circulates.
The road's rule and the house's rule cannot both hold and neither derives from the other: standing on the road is earned by crossing, and the house's exclusivity is published and unfalsifiable.

The unanswered petition asks which of two published exclusivities governs a traveller's cloth, and this household is one of the two publishers. It has never answered, because answering would be a price.

The league of the two coasts exists so both shores can admit they need each other without either conceding the water, and a household that publishes discretion is the only member that can be on both banks without conceding anything.
The terraces are engraved absences visible from the district below, so a refusal that has run two generations is physically legible from the ground and cannot be quietly amended.

The ancestor paid one period of upkeep on an immortal seat and then stopped. The arrears were never released, which is why the border is still crossed one person at a time and why this household still appears on a tally.
Self-appointment, judging one's own trial and reading a vacancy as a zero are all prohibited, and this household cannot discharge a refusal without doing one of the three.

The council decides who may step onto the terraces and cannot be a candidate for any of them, so it is structurally the only body that could clear this account and structurally forbidden from being paid for doing so.
The office names the unfilled high seats and is forbidden to take them, so this household's refusal is a line in a register maintained by the one institution that cannot profit from filling it.

Upkeep goes from half a unit to as many as five across the border, so a crossing that costs more than a life returns and a seat held for one period is a seat nobody can keep. The refusal is the arithmetic, not the mood.

The underwriter sells cover against a road closing, which no market can price because no tier below the spirit frame has a season. This marriage network is the instrument that makes the cover possible.

An old seafaring trading culture that has never recovered a price list, and this network is what that refusal looks like when it has to be renewed by somebody: six marriages standing in for a table of rates.
Risk in both directions means neither house has to hold enough unpriced cover to survive a bad season, which is the one thing exclusivity would have forced both of them to do.

Cloth and cut identify what a traveller is and what they may open, because the only thing anybody controls is permission to pass. A network of marriages between houses is itself a credential, and it is worn the same way.
Elemental law is unwritten in the mortal tier, so nobody can forecast anything and insurance is the only instrument left for the unknown. Remove the absence and the marriages are sentimental.
A salt dominion cannot move its population up the shore without ceasing to be the people it governs, so its households are bound to a waterline and to each other.
Nobody here is inside or outside, only high, low or turning, so a marriage booked to an anchor is the ordinary way a union is recorded in a place whose clock is two tides a day.

The crossing window is set by the season rather than by the holder's preference, so the weeks worth having are a public fact four households are arguing over, and a wedding is how a household claims one.

The spirit tier's inland sea holds its shape because spatial law is written here and keeps time because temporal law is, which is the first place a date can be trusted enough to be worth marrying against.
A league is the only form that lets both shores admit they need each other without either conceding the water, and a calendar shared by four households is the same bargain made in a smaller room.

The pass is re-surveyed every period and a booking is a survey made years in advance, so the line that holds the ground and the households that fix the dates are the same arrangement seen from two ends.
The anchored season is what this tier can have only because elemental law is written here, and without an anchor there is no window, no best weeks and nothing to marry against.
The abandoned crossing and its bed of unmortared seats sit at realm eighteen, the last spirit gate, where the cost of existing changes character and upkeep goes from half a unit to as many as five.

A seat cannot be held by somebody who cannot pay for it every period, so the attempt left a bed of unusable seats. Holding the far end of a crossing that cannot happen is the only office the residue affords.
The office sells standing on the bed and is unmortarable because nobody attempted the crossing could afford the upkeep, so these households are the only parties who actually stand there.

One seat is vacant because its heirs were culled and one because it has no powers to confer and an empty successor parameter to read. These wardens keep both on the same tally so neither is read as a zero.

The same failure seen from two ends: one household stands at a crossing that cannot happen, the other cannot pay for a seat that was filled once. Neither can discharge the account and both are cited on it.
A crossing that costs more than a life returns, and what returns is a seat nobody can pay for. This wardenship is the standing consequence of the tariff being the only wealth there is.

Realm eighteen is an economic bottleneck before it is a spiritual one, and most of the people who never reached it were below realm nine and never knew the border existed. These households are staffed by people who found out anyway.

This is the only place in the setting where a law is written twice and the second writing wins, so anything that must not fail is built here. A ground like that needs a keeper and cannot afford a proprietor.
The shelf is the layer made real ground, so the household is custodian of a duplicate rather than of a place, and its tenure is measured in imprints held unspent.
A slot is one law written at one value into one layer, which is why ten seats over six groups is four duplicates rather than four spare laws. The household exists to hold what the budget cannot use.

A strained law is observed only where it is written twice and read against itself, and this is the only ground where that comparison is physically available. Keeping the surface is how the reading survives.
The Court is the first tier with a second layer, so the surplus law rises through the district rather than being argued about above it. These households are what it rises through.

One carries the imprints that exist twice and the other administers the seats that are spare and empty; each is the other's standing argument that the count is wrong, and neither can be closed without losing the surface.
Changes of name held collectively, letters read and never kept, and a funeral nobody may attend without losing standing. This lineage is the household form of a practice designed to be uncitable.

The anchorage was added to the settlement the caravan collapse left, and a community that will not accept exclusivity has to become impossible to enumerate. A lineage that keeps no roll is the smallest unit that achieves that.

A member's share of any unsettled claim is transferred at the next re-drawing in front of the community and cannot be contested afterwards, which is the only inheritance instrument that works on a lineage with no register.

A people who hold no written record and retire their names annually cannot be cited, so the writ's entire instrument is unavailable to them and its only answer is to deny the pass. This lineage lives downstream of that answer.

The league is a trade body, and a trade body has to be able to describe its counterparties, which is exactly the thing this lineage is built to avoid. The trade continues because the league cannot prove who it traded with.
Two families that exist because they are not on a roll, arguing about which roll they refuse. One is unlisted by choice and one by law, and neither will accept the other's reason.

The only standing force on the plains is paid out of the ring's take and posted at the foot of the stair, and a child of the levy who is entered nowhere is the only kind of body it can hold without owning.
The one graded route out of the Mortal Plains, and the only departure the ascent ever used, so the households that raise the called are the ones at the only door the setting has.

The Marshal may close the river crossings and call the levy, and the levy is answered by people who may say no. That only works if the marshalled are not already subjects, so these households raise what the March may not own.

The Marshal's three stages are sworn at the ford, hold the bridge, and be named by the March, in that order and never another. A raised child is the second stage before anybody has decided they will take the first.
The claim is written only by a completed trial and moved only by ford dues actually settled, so a called child is standing and never owing, and neither number is this household's to move.
The writ keeps debts of access rather than money at the one pass that crosses the ridge, and a household that raises the uncountable is exactly the population its instrument cannot reach.

A salt dominion's territory is exactly its waterline and the specialised body that can drink it stops above the brine line, so the only ground this house can hold is the one its own chemistry makes habitable. The sea is the boundary it lives on and cannot cross.

The oldest recorded carrier line descends from this one household, kept unbroken because two generations of pure pairing is the ceiling of any chain and nothing else reaches it. The land is incidental; the chain is the estate.
The line's reading is tide-born and the household's refusal to marry out is what keeps the reading legible; every marriage that would have diluted it also diluted the race survey it is filed under.

The college keeps no second copy: the list exists in one reader's head until the reading. This household's record begins after the culls, so the oldest surviving carrier entry it holds is also the entry that cannot establish priority.

Two records of one origin, one of them arithmetic and one of them a memory, and no authority in the setting entitled to decide between them. This household knows it holds a memory and has never been able to make it a proof.

The competing claim to the oldest carrier line. One is a memory that begins late; the other has no household at all. Neither can be certified and the disagreement is the only inheritance either of them can point to.
Two houses whose entire function is refusing to dilute a line, one by crossing once and never again and one by never crossing at all. Both hold a thin concentration as a deliberate asset.
A fire-affinity line is only an asset where elemental law is written, so this household's crossing was made for the one valley that could use it and the descendants are useless everywhere else.

The founding concentration descends from this household's single mineral-fire crossing. It was made once at a founding generation and never repeated, which is why the concentration is thin, unevenly spread and defensive rather than large.
The ley is where fire has ground to act on below the spirit tier, so a founding-generation fire affinity was carried here first and the household stayed where its one useful crossing still is.
Elemental, spatial and temporal are never written in a mortal tier, so a fire-affinity body has nothing to spend into and the whole discipline of this household is containment rather than use.

The one conception was shared with the mineral-fire line and never repeated, so the pressure-resistance in the descendant is the only half of the crossing that survived. A second crossing would average it into the general population.
One house refuses to cross a second time and the other refuses to cross at all; both spend their whole substance on a thin line that a single well-meant marriage would dissolve.
The ordinary body is the one this household averages into itself, and a household whose only distinction is reliability has to be everywhere because nowhere is it exceptional.

The default concentration is carried carefully for many generations and averaged with whatever the household took in. It is inherited as a practice, not as a property, so it needs a house that keeps doing it.
The commons of a frame seating three laws is judged by what survives the season, and this is the household that keeps the most of its members surviving it.
A tenure-queue household that has held its slot long enough to have generations is where a kept, averaged concentration starts. Nothing about it is exceptional except that it was not interrupted.
A hundred-year body and a ceiling of eight realms on ground that cannot hold a measurement, so this household's whole competence is the season.
The Assembly meets at the crossing rather than beside it, and a household that averages whatever it took in has nothing to declare when it gets there.

The obvious reading nobody may certify: a cull narrows a pool enough to cross the founding bar and destroys the record of what was culled, which would make this line a debt somebody else's descendants are still paying. Recorded as the claim, not as the finding.

A cull is a political act and never an anatomical one, so the narrowed pool may cross any race and no record survives to say whose it was. That is the only mechanism in the book that could produce a line this narrow with no parent.

Two records of one origin and no authority entitled to decide between them. This line has the arithmetic and no household; that household has the oldest surviving carrier entry and a record that begins after the culls.

A line with no recorded origin and no household that will admit to it, whose founding bar leaves exactly one generation of pure-by-pure inheritance able to clear it. This is the only claim on that line anybody has ever filed.
The culture of households that culled their own branches and bound every survivor to a named debt. Any household living under this line would be one, and none will say so.
The shelf's households had already been crossed with outsiders when the cull ran, so the ground is where a mixed pool would be recorded and the record is precisely what is missing.

This is the standing objection to that line, made by people who are not its descendants: the bar must be clearable by somebody for the ladder to be worth climbing, and no household may admit the body that clears it.

The refusal is only enforceable while the bar is unclaimed. The instant a household enters the clearing body for the record, the founding line is owned and this household's founding rule has nothing left to refuse.

A competing claim needs somebody to be claiming. These households refuse the claim on purpose, which is the only reason the arithmetic and the memory can both stay on the table without either being settled.
The only resource nobody can corner, whose holders have nothing to gain from a war, is the one place a household whose standing is refusal pays nothing to hold.

The lodge sells bodies already tuned to the frame on the far side of a tear. These households cannot follow a member across a boundary without breaking their own rule, which is exactly the traffic the lodge exists for.

The bill for opening a world was written in law seats and no surviving record names the payer. A household whose founding practice is not to record is the one custom the missing payer could plausibly have used.

A community needing a guarantee of welcome cannot get one from the world and has to mark its own threshold. A house that is forbidden to record has to mark something instead, and the threshold is what survives.
The same fifty-year arithmetic produced both: this house signs every child to a furnace and the marked household holds every table to a rule. Neither of them expects the shortage to end.

One network books a wedding against a season and one house signs a child against a furnace before it is named. Both are ways of tying a life to a date the family does not control, and only one of them is survivable at a fifty-year body.

Fire affinity is worthless on the plains and an asset in Flame Valley, and the valley is past the pass the ration house keeps fed. Neither supply is any use without the other, so neither house can refuse the other.

A maximally dense fixed body is the subject of the ceiling, and the ceiling is what made the species: this household exists to employ one at seventeen instead of losing it at nineteen to a gate that will not open.

The relic is useless without somebody who can hold a forge at full weight, and a seventeen-year body is the only one that can. The wardens answer one question a year; the house of stopped bodies supplies the hands.

A failed ascent injures the ground and leaves a body that stopped at seventeen with nobody to teach, so the register household can only feed an intake it cannot place without a house that takes competent strangers whole.
The Regent may name a seat and may not take one, and every appointment goes through a trial the Regent cannot judge. This household is the reason that sentence was worth writing down twice.

One holds the crop the absent left a claim to and the other counts the absent's children as lost. The claim and the departure are the same money, so the two houses have been settling it for two generations.

The famine fell hardest on the households holding the longest tenure, because a tenure-queue family keeps more members alive to starve than a household that can leave. This is where the scar's ordinary line runs.

Both keep names of people who are not here. One has a river that moves and a charter that recognises the claim; the other has a border that cannot be crossed and an office that cannot be held. Neither arrangement answers the other's question.

A duplicate imprint has to be carried by somebody the Court can name and cannot promote, which is the same construction as the highest office and the reason this household can be trusted with surface law.

A salt-and-tide body is the only one that can stand on both shores of the league's routes, so the marriage network between the counting houses and the underwriters draws its participants from one crossing.
The long line still carries the most common concentration in the setting, averaged like any other settled household. Three centuries of life has not made it rarer, only slower to replace.

The grant trades immediate impact for sustained pressure because the line was held unbroken, and it is held unbroken because holding it is the household's only function. The line and the house are the same asset counted twice.

The league of the two coasts formed the moment the sea became worth owning, and this household is on the waterline it governs. It is a member because a house that will not dilute its line can still be part of a trade league, and refusing the league would cost it the one road it has.

The sterile ground around the seam is spoil that has not moved in four decades because nothing on the plains can carry it away. A claim on a dead deposit survives because the ruin outlives everyone who remembers the working, and that ruin is the only witness this household has.

The seam is a gradient rather than a pocket, so the cleft is a falling series of thin, hard, increasingly deep workings and every one of them needs feeding before it can be worked. The ration contract exists because the mine moves downward and the food does not.

The kelp grows to the tideline and stops the moment the Tidemark turns against it, so the whole food base of this sea is a calendar. Booking a marriage against that calendar is booking it against an organism, which is why the network argues about weeks rather than dates.
